title: The Midnight Gala
setting: Hale Gallery, a private art gallery, during its 20th anniversary gala.
victim: Edmund Hale, founder and owner of Hale Gallery
briefing: At 23:05 a waiter found Edmund Hale dead in his upstairs study, struck down with a heavy object. Guests were downstairs all evening. Four people had a reason to be near him tonight. Find out who did it.

topic_labels.victim: What was Edmund Hale to you?
topic_labels.painting: What do you know about the Dutch Landscape?
topic_labels.vivian: What do you make of Vivian Cross?

suspects.name: Vivian Cross
suspects.personality: Polished, warm, and always in control of the room.
suspects.background: Co-founded the gallery with Edmund twenty years ago and runs its finances.
suspects.motive: Edmund found out she sold the real Dutch Landscape and hid 40,000 from the books.
suspects.secret: She killed Edmund in his study at about 22:40.

statements.text: I gave the toast at half past nine and never left the ballroom after that. Ask anyone.
Edmund and I built this gallery together. We were like family.
The books are in perfect order. Edmund never touched the accounts.

reactions.text: Oh, that. I went up the service stairs to fetch my shawl. A two minute errand, nothing more.

reveals.text: Fine, I slipped upstairs once to fetch my shawl and came straight back. I saw nothing.

reactions.text: Half the gala wears lavender. You cannot pin this on me.

suspects.name: Marcus Hale
suspects.personality: Charming, nervous, and quick to joke when cornered.
suspects.background: Works odd jobs, owes money to people he should not.
suspects.motive: He inherits a large share of the estate and has heavy gambling debts.
suspects.secret: He went upstairs at 22:00 to beg Edmund for money and they argued.

statements.text: I was at the bar all evening. I never went upstairs.
My uncle was generous when it suited him.
Yes, I owe people. The will would help me, but I would never hurt him.

reveals.text: I went up at ten to ask Uncle for money. We shouted. He was alive and furious when I left at ten past.

suspects.name: Elena Voss
suspects.personality: Precise, quiet, and honest to the point of bluntness.
suspects.background: Authenticates every major piece the gallery sells.
suspects.motive: She feared the gallery's reputation, and her own, would be ruined by a forgery scandal.
suspects.secret: She discovered the Dutch Landscape on display is a fake.

statements.text: I was in the cellar storage room from quarter past ten until five to eleven, examining the Dutch Landscape.
Edmund trusted my eye over anyone's.
The Dutch Landscape on the wall is a forgery. The real one was sold and replaced. I told Edmund last week.
Vivian always wears that lavender hand cream. You can smell it across a room.

suspects.name: Tomas Reyes
suspects.personality: Nervous, polite, and desperate not to lose his job.
suspects.background: Has run the gallery's events for six years.
suspects.motive: Edmund once threatened to fire him over missing wine.
suspects.secret: He sneaked a bottle from the cellar at 22:24 and saw Vivian heading up the service stairs.

statements.text: I was in the kitchen running the service line all night.
Mr. Hale was a fair employer.

reactions.text: Please do not tell the owners...

reveals.text: I slipped down for a bottle of the 98. On my way back, around half past ten, I saw Ms. Cross in the service corridor heading for the stairs.

evidence.name: Smashed wristwatch
evidence.description: Edmund's watch, stopped at 22:41. It was crushed when he fell.

evidence.name: Bronze falcon statuette
evidence.description: A heavy statuette that was wiped clean. A faint lavender scent clings to it.

evidence.name: Torn ledger page
evidence.description: Edmund's handwriting: 'V.C. - Dutch Landscape sale, 40k not in the books. Confront tonight.'

evidence.name: Gold cufflink
evidence.description: A monogrammed cufflink under the desk, engraved with the letters M.H.

evidence.name: Gala program card
evidence.description: Lists Vivian Cross's toast from 21:30 to 21:45 and nothing after.

evidence.name: Cellar sign-out sheet
evidence.description: Shows Elena Voss signed in at 22:15, and a bottle of 1998 red signed out at 22:24 by T. Reyes.

evidence.name: Service door keycard log
evidence.description: Vivian Cross's keycard opened the service stair door at 22:32 going up and at 22:46 going down.

timeline.text: Vivian gives her toast in the ballroom.
The toast ends. Vivian leaves the stage.
Marcus goes up to the study and argues with Edmund about money.
Marcus storms out. Edmund is alive.
Elena goes down to the cellar to examine the Dutch Landscape.
Tomas takes a bottle from the cellar.
Vivian uses the service stairs to go up to the study.
Vivian kills Edmund with the statuette.
Vivian returns downstairs by the service stairs.

solution.motive: Edmund discovered she sold the real Dutch Landscape and hid 40,000 from the books.
solution.method: She struck Edmund with the bronze statuette in his study and wiped it clean.
solution.explanation: Vivian claimed she never left the ballroom, but her keycard opened the service stairs at 22:32 up and 22:46 down, which brackets the time Edmund's watch stopped at 22:41. The statuette smells of the lavender cream only she wears, and Edmund's torn ledger page shows she had a motive to silence him. Marcus argued with Edmund but left at 22:10 while he was still alive, and Elena and Tomas were in the cellar.
